cases.translation: The performance was in full swing.
cases.explain: «Спектакль» is the subject of «был» (was), so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: Разговор о лошадях занимал его, но ни на минуту он не забывал ___.
cases.translation: The conversation about horses occupied him, but not for a minute did he forget Anna.
cases.explain: The negated verb «не забывал» requires the Genitive case for its object: «не забывал Анны».

cases.sentence: Варя подала руку ___ и тотчас же начала говорить с ним о том, что интересовало его.
cases.translation: Varya gave her hand to her brother-in-law and immediately began speaking with him about what interested him.
cases.explain: The verb «подала» (gave) takes an indirect object in the Dative case: «подала руку деверю».

cases.sentence: Вронский вошел в ___ в половине девятого.
cases.translation: Vronsky entered the theater at half past eight.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing motion into a place governs the Accusative case: «в театр».

cases.sentence: ...он прошел до первого ряда и остановился у рампы с ___, который, согнув колено и постукивая каблуком в рампу, подозвал к себе улыбкой.
cases.translation: ...he walked up to the front row and stopped by the footlights with Serpukhovskoy, who, bending his knee and tapping his heel against the footlights, beckoned him over with a smile.
cases.explain: The preposition «с» (with) governs the Instrumental case: «с Серпуховским».

cases.sentence: ...напомнили ему ее такую совершенно, какую он увидел ее на бале в ___.
cases.translation: ...reminded him of her exactly as he had seen her at the ball in Moscow.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» (in) governs the Prepositional case: «в Москве».

reading.ru: Вронский в первый раз испытывал против Анны чувство досады, почти злобы за ее умышленное непонимание своего положения.
reading.question: What feeling did Vronsky experience toward Anna for the first time?
options: Vexation, almost anger, at her willful failure to understand her position
reading.correct: Vexation, almost anger, at her willful failure to understand her position
reading.explain: The text says Vronsky for the first time felt vexation, almost anger, toward Anna for her deliberate failure to understand her position.

reading.ru: «Это лошадь хорошая, и я советую тебе купить», — сказал Яшвин, оглянув мрачное лицо товарища.
reading.question: What did Yashvin advise Vronsky to buy?
reading.correct: A good horse
reading.explain: Yashvin tells Vronsky it is a good horse and he advises him to buy it.

reading.ru: Анна Аркадьевна приказала доложить, что они поехали в театр.
reading.question: What message did Anna send about the evening's plans?
options: That they had gone to the theater
That she would meet him later
That she had left for the countryside
reading.correct: That they had gone to the theater
reading.explain: The text says Anna Arkadyevna sent word that they had gone to the theater.

reading.ru: «Я не поеду», — мрачно отвечал Вронский.
reading.question: How did Vronsky respond when Yashvin asked if he was coming to the theater?
options: He said gloomily that he would not go
He asked Yashvin to wait for him
He said he had already been
reading.correct: He said gloomily that he would not go
reading.explain: Vronsky answers gloomily, 'I am not going.'

reading.ru: Этим движением он зацепил столик, на котором стояла сельтерская вода и графин с коньяком, и чуть не столкнул его.
reading.question: What happened when Vronsky angrily waved his hand?
options: He knocked against a table with seltzer water and a decanter of brandy
He spilled ink on some papers
reading.correct: He knocked against a table with seltzer water and a decanter of brandy
reading.explain: The text says this motion caught a little table holding seltzer water and a brandy decanter, nearly knocking it over.

reading.ru: Камердинер, чувствуя себя невиноватым, хотел оправдываться, но, взглянув на барина, понял по его лицу, что надо только молчать,
reading.question: How did the valet react to Vronsky's anger?
options: He wanted to defend himself but realized from Vronsky's face that he should stay silent
reading.correct: He wanted to defend himself but realized from Vronsky's face that he should stay silent
reading.explain: The valet, feeling not at fault, wanted to justify himself, but seeing his master's face, understood he should only keep silent.

reading.ru: Вронский вошел в театр в половине девятого.
reading.question: At what time did Vronsky arrive at the theater?
reading.correct: Half past eight
reading.explain: The text states Vronsky entered the theater at half past eight.

reading.ru: На сцене певица, блестя обнаженными плечами и бриллиантами, нагибаясь и улыбаясь, собирала с помощью тенора, державшего ее за руку, неловко перелетавшие через рампу букеты,
reading.question: What was happening on stage when Vronsky entered the hall?
options: A singer, glittering with bare shoulders and diamonds, was gathering bouquets thrown onto the stage
reading.correct: A singer, glittering with bare shoulders and diamonds, was gathering bouquets thrown onto the stage
reading.explain: The text describes a singer, gleaming with bare shoulders and diamonds, gathering bouquets that had awkwardly flown over the footlights.

reading.ru: Вронский вошел в середину портера и, остановившись, стал оглядываться.
reading.question: What did Vronsky do after entering the stalls?
options: He stood in the middle and looked around
He left through a side door
reading.correct: He stood in the middle and looked around
reading.explain: The text says Vronsky walked into the middle of the stalls and, stopping, began to look around.

reading.ru: На его счастье, Алексея Александровича нынешний раз не было в театре.
reading.question: What fortunate detail did Vronsky notice about Karenin?
options: Karenin was not at the theater that evening
reading.correct: Karenin was not at the theater that evening
reading.explain: The text says luckily for him, Alexei Alexandrovich was not at the theater this time.

reading.ru: «Как в тебе мало осталось военного!» — сказал ему Серпуховской.
reading.question: What did Serpukhovskoy remark to Vronsky about his appearance?
options: That little of the military man remained in him
reading.correct: That little of the military man remained in him
reading.explain: Serpukhovskoy tells him how little of the military man is left in him.

reading.ru: Вронский вдруг увидал голову Анны, гордую, поразительно красивую и улыбающуюся в рамке кружев.
reading.question: How did Vronsky describe Anna's appearance when he spotted her in the box?
options: Proud, strikingly beautiful, and smiling in a frame of lace
reading.correct: Proud, strikingly beautiful, and smiling in a frame of lace
reading.explain: The text says Vronsky suddenly saw Anna's head, proud, strikingly beautiful, and smiling within a frame of lace.

reading.ru: Она была в пятом бенуаре, в двадцати шагах от него.
reading.question: Where was Anna seated in the theater?
options: In the fifth baignoire, twenty paces from him
In the front row of the stalls
reading.correct: In the fifth baignoire, twenty paces from him
reading.explain: The text says she was in the fifth baignoire, twenty paces away from him.

reading.ru: Когда Вронский опять навел в ту сторону бинокль, он заметил, что княжна Варвара особенно красна, неестественно смеется и беспрестанно оглядывается на соседнюю ложу.
reading.question: What did Vronsky notice about Princess Varvara through his opera glasses?
options: She looked flushed, laughed unnaturally, and kept glancing at the neighboring box
She had left the box entirely
reading.correct: She looked flushed, laughed unnaturally, and kept glancing at the neighboring box
reading.explain: The text says he noticed Princess Varvara was especially flushed, laughing unnaturally, and constantly glancing at the next box.

reading.ru: Картасова, худая маленькая женщина, стояла в своей ложе и, спиной обратившись к Анне, надевала накидку, подаваемую ей мужем.
reading.question: What did Madame Kartasova do in her box, with her back turned to Anna?
options: She put on a wrap handed to her by her husband
She left immediately without a word
reading.correct: She put on a wrap handed to her by her husband
reading.explain: The text says Kartasova, a thin small woman, stood in her box with her back to Anna, putting on a wrap her husband handed her.

reading.ru: Он понял это и потому, что видел, и более всего, по лицу Анны, которая, он знал, собрала свои последние силы, чтобы выдерживать взятую на себя роль.
reading.question: How did Vronsky know something humiliating had happened to Anna?
options: Mostly from Anna's face, which showed she was gathering her last strength to maintain her composed role
Someone told him directly what happened
He read a note passed to him
Anna wept openly in the box
reading.correct: Mostly from Anna's face, which showed she was gathering her last strength to maintain her composed role
reading.explain: He understood it partly from what he saw, and most of all from Anna's face, which showed she had gathered her last strength to keep up the role she had taken on.

reading.ru: Мне муж рассказал. Она оскорбила Каренину.
reading.question: What did Varya tell Vronsky had happened, according to what her husband told her?
options: Madame Kartasova had insulted Anna Karenina
The theater manager had removed Anna
reading.correct: Madame Kartasova had insulted Anna Karenina
reading.explain: Varya says her husband told her that Kartasova had insulted Karenina.

reading.ru: Я нахожу, что это низко и гадко, и мадам Картасова не имела никакого права.
reading.question: What was Varya's opinion of Madame Kartasova's behavior?
options: She found it base and vile, and felt Madame Kartasova had no right to act that way
She thought it was a fair response
She refused to comment on it
reading.correct: She found it base and vile, and felt Madame Kartasova had no right to act that way
reading.explain: Varya says she finds it low and vile, and that Madame Kartasova had no right to do it.

reading.ru: «А я тебя все жду», сказала ему мать, насмешливо улыбаясь.
reading.question: How did Vronsky's mother greet him when he entered the box?
options: She said she had been waiting for him, smiling mockingly
She scolded him for being late
She introduced him to a stranger
reading.correct: She said she had been waiting for him, smiling mockingly
reading.explain: His mother says, 'And I've been waiting for you all this time,' smiling mockingly.

reading.ru: «Маман, я вас просил не говорить мне про это», — отвечал он, хмурясь.
reading.question: How did Vronsky respond when his mother teased him about courting Anna Karenina?
options: He frowned and asked her not to speak to him about it
He laughed and agreed with her
He left the box without a word
reading.correct: He frowned and asked her not to speak to him about it
reading.explain: Vronsky answers, frowning, 'Maman, I have asked you not to speak to me about this.'

reading.ru: Он сошел вниз в портер и направился прямо к Бенуару Анны.
reading.question: Where did Vronsky go after leaving his brother's box?
options: Down to the stalls and straight to Anna's baignoire
reading.correct: Down to the stalls and straight to Anna's baignoire
reading.explain: The text says he went down to the stalls and headed straight to Anna's baignoire.

reading.ru: «Я плохой ценитель», — сказал он, строго глядя на нее.
reading.question: How did Vronsky respond when Anna mockingly asked if he had heard the best aria?
options: He said he was a poor judge, looking sternly at her
He agreed enthusiastically about the aria
He changed the subject to Yashvin's horse
reading.correct: He said he was a poor judge, looking sternly at her
reading.explain: Vronsky answers, 'I am a poor judge,' looking sternly at her.

reading.ru: И вдруг в это мгновение красивое лицо ее вздрогнуло. Она встала и пошла вглубь ложи.
reading.question: What did Anna suddenly do while speaking with Vronsky and Stremov?
options: Her beautiful face trembled, and she stood up and walked to the back of the box
She invited Stremov to sit closer
reading.correct: Her beautiful face trembled, and she stood up and walked to the back of the box
reading.explain: The text says her beautiful face suddenly trembled, and she rose and walked to the back of the box.

reading.ru: «Ты! Ты виноват во всем!» — вскрикнула она со слезами отчаяния и злости в голосе, вставая.
reading.question: What did Anna cry out when Vronsky came to her at home?
options: That he was to blame for everything
That she wanted to leave him
That she wanted to return to Karenin
reading.correct: That he was to blame for everything
reading.explain: Anna cries out, 'You! You are to blame for everything!' rising with tears of despair and anger in her voice.

reading.ru: На другой день после этого, совершенно примиренные, они уехали в деревню.
reading.question: How did the chapter end?
options: The next day, completely reconciled, they left for the countryside
reading.correct: The next day, completely reconciled, they left for the countryside
reading.explain: The text says the next day, fully reconciled, they departed for the country.
